resolutions: Any well-formed typed verbstem remains open input; Canvas examples do not form a stem whitelist.
A formula example proves its morpheme shape and relation rather than authorizing only the printed stem.
The applicative adds a participant tangential to the Source event through the shared derivation owner.
Inherent-applicative, irregular, or valence-neutral Source analysis is selected only when the intended lexical analysis cannot be derived.
Maca preserves its inherent-applicative analysis automatically when that typed Source analysis is supplied.
Itzi and itta histories remain distinct typed Source analyses without restricting either route to a stored example list.
Object depth, mainline status, governor, and participant transfer follow the typed Source and applicative operation automatically.
Honorific-only and example-meaning observations remain reading guidance rather than controls.
Type 1 availability is a genuine lexical choice for an open typed Source because it is not predictable from spelling alone.
Type 1 replaces the final Source vowel with ia and derives the resulting boundary changes automatically.
Class C membership and the imported applicative object are consequences of the selected Type 1 operation.
Causative versus Applicative is exposed only when both roles remain possible for the intended final composition.
Visible homophony cannot silently choose a derivational role.
Type 2 and its intended applicative participant are genuine final-composition choices.
Typed Source shape, class, and signed history select lia or huia whenever those facts already determine the route.
A Source-history choice appears only when more than one licensed route remains after typed provenance is considered.
Final-i lengthening and the si-to-xi and tzi-or-ti-to-chi changes are automatic shape effects.
A retained Source reflexive moves to shuntline ne through the shared participant owner.
Ayi preserves its grammatically present silent third-person specific object when an applicative participant is added.
The silent ayi object stays structurally available on the shuntline and never becomes a separate sounded-versus-silent control.
Applicative object ordering and sounded realization use the canonical object-cluster machinery rather than atom-specific code.
Clickable cues report Source history, boundary change, derivation role, participant depth, and silence without becoming grammar authority.
Reader-only atoms explain the accepted structure and cannot authorize, select, or rewrite a formation.
Mutation checks contradict each accepted writing job independently while normal application observations remain exact.
An open typed final-a Source receives every route licensed by its shape and signed history without example-stem admission.
Final ia loses its last vowel and receives lia automatically.
A consonant-plus-a Source changes final a to i before lia through the shared shape rule.
The ca-to-qui, sa-to-xi, and tla-or-tza-to-chi outcomes are derived boundary effects rather than controls.
The exact occasional tla-to-ti route stays a narrow lexical overlay and does not block the productive neighboring rule.
A completed applicative may be recaptured as a typed Source for another applicative through the normal derivation path.
Recursive applicativization imports one new participant while preserving earlier object levels automatically.
The user chooses a final-a Source history or recursive structure only when more than one licensed analysis remains.
Class D final long a preserves that vowel and appends lia for any matching open typed Source.
A transitive Class B iya Source appends lia, while an intransitive Class B eya Source deletes ya before lia.
The iya and eya exception routes use typed class, shape, and valence rather than a Canvas stem list.
An intransitive oya Source deletes ya before lia, while a transitive oya Source preserves the whole Source and appends lia.
Oya transitivity is a genuine Source analysis choice only when the intended composition has not already fixed valence.
Class, vowel preservation, ya deletion, suffix choice, and target Class C are automatic consequences.
A root-final l plus o-a Source derives huiā automatically from its visible typed internal morphology.
A root-final o plus causative a Source derives l-huiā automatically when that internal boundary is typed.
Signed earlier causative history recovers a-hui, i-hui, o-hui, or root-plus-ya provenance without presenting a new menu.
An unresolved consonant-final o-a Source presents only the licensed internal-history alternatives.
Selecting an unresolved internal history derives the reconstructed base, fusion, huiā, and participant structure automatically.
The exceptional tēm-o-ā to tēm-o-liā route remains a narrow lexical exception rather than a productive spelling rule.
The iht-o-ā to il-huiā route remains genuine suppletion and does not create an iht-to-il rewrite for other stems.
Exact exception and suppletion records coexist with open productive shape rules without turning the witness inventory into a whitelist.
Clickable final-a, exception, and o-a or huiā cues expose the typed reason for the Result without authorizing it.
Formula spelling, editorial boundaries, and example meanings remain reading evidence when the canonical morpheme relation is unchanged.
Final-long-o applicatives use the same licensed direct or replacive huia shape as the parallel causative without letting surface identity choose the derivational role.
The rare tia applicative routes consume their typed nonactive Source history and remain narrow exceptions rather than productive spelling rewrites.
Parallel Type 1 and Type 2 applicatives remain separate choices when both are licensed for the intended final composition.
Every selected Type 1, Type 2, or rare Type 3 applicative derives Class C and imports its participant through the shared participant transform.
Canvas meanings and contextual interpretations explain special and parallel Results but never authorize, suppress, or whitelist a stem.
An intransitive Source plus an applicative participant derives exactly one target object without a manual valence control.
Nonspecific-human, specific-projective, and reflexive applicative participants use the ordinary object-kind and identity choices.
The Source subject is preserved and the added applicative object receives its carrier, governor, level, and mainline status automatically.
Adverbial embedding, tla fusion, plural agreement, and witnessed meanings remain automatic structure or reading evidence rather than extra controls.
A single-object Source plus an applicative participant derives exactly two target objects through the same open applicative operation.
The newest applicative object becomes mainline and the retained Source object becomes shuntline according to derivational level.
Specific-object incompatibility and partial or full silence are derived by the canonical object cluster rather than exposed as applicative controls.
A retained Source reflexive automatically becomes nonfirst-common shuntline ne unless a narrow lexical exception is independently authorized.
Prefix order follows participant type and derivational history and cannot be manually rearranged.
A grammatically present silent Source object remains eligible for the ordinary Lesson 17 supplementation relation.
The user chooses a supplement head only when multiple eligible silent heads remain; referent contact, hierarchy, and the supplement link are otherwise derived.
An eligible double-object Result can be recaptured as the typed Source of another applicative without a separate triple-object engine.
The newest applicative participant becomes the third-level mainline object and the two earlier objects remain first- and second-level shuntlines.
Triple-object compatibility, silence, ne, and prefix order are derived by the ordinary object-cluster machinery.
Only the recaptured Source, added participant, and genuine referent identity remain user choices in recursive applicative composition.
A silent earlier object remains grammatically present and eligible for ordinary supplementation after another applicative layer.
Typed Source history preserves licensed object-role interpretations even when the visible prefix sequence does not distinguish them.
Surface spelling never selects among competing applicative Source analyses.
A Source interpretation is chosen only when later composition or actual context requires resolution.
Wish, command or exhortation, and admonition use the shared Mood owner after applicative formation.
Passive and impersonal applicatives use the shared Voice owner and preserve every licensed retained participant.
English translation difficulty does not alter the typed participant hierarchy or grammatical Voice.
Human, nonhuman, reflexive, and specific applicative participants use the ordinary participant-kind control only where a real alternative remains.
Fixed participant interpretations follow typed Source structure automatically and do not create extra menus.
Same-looking forms may retain distinct typed Source analyses without treating their surface as grammar authority.
Causative and applicative routes remain separate typed compositions even when their Results or English translations are close.
The applicative object and applicative derivational suffix remain one discontinuous grammatical unit.
Canvas witness stems and English glosses remain reading evidence and never gate open Source input.
Clickable recursive, ambiguity, Mood, Voice, interpretation, and suffix-link cues report owner-issued structure without authorizing it.
